text:
Recent research supports measuring branch gradients rather than interpreting loss weights as learning allocation. [Recon](https://arxiv.org/abs/2302.11289) localizes conflict by layer; [GCond (2025–2026)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2509.07252) investigates accumulation-based gradient stabilization and computational cost. [JMLR 2024](https://www.jmlr.org/beta/papers/v25/23-1287.html) establishes trade-offs between conflict avoidance, optimization and generalization: negative gradient cosine alone does not establish harmful transfer. [Masked History Learning (2025–2026)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2509.23649) combines historical reconstruction with next-item prediction in generative recommendation, but does not validate the specific 0.75/0.25 weighting for BERT4Rec.

Suggested read-only adaptation: on a small, fixed training-batch panel, compute terminal and reconstruction gradients separately with `autograd.grad`, without optimizer steps. For embeddings and each encoder layer, report unweighted norms, weighted norms (0.75‖g_terminal‖, 0.25‖g_reconstruction‖), cosine, negative-dot-product frequency, and combined-gradient norm. These are sensitivity diagnostics; AdamW’s actual update also depends on optimizer state. Preserve exact implemented loss numerators and denominators: ordinary unweighted cross-entropy means exclude ignored targets, while class weighting changes the denominator ([PyTorch documentation](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/generated/torch.nn.CrossEntropyLoss.html)). A 75% scalar coefficient does not imply 75% gradient contribution.

For sampling-noise diagnosis, estimate gradient variance across batches at one frozen checkpoint; repeat histories with fixed versus resampled masks to separate masking variability, controlling dropout. Persistent negative alignment suggests interference; unstable signs with high variance suggest sampling noise, without proving causality. Proposed provenance: checkpoint hash, category, parameter groups, batch/mask seeds, model mode, loss reductions, valid-target counts and formulas. Flag zero-norm cosines, undefined denominators, mismatched checkpoints, and any claimed allocation unsupported by measured norms. This preserves the single model and fixed objective.
